title: Percy Grainger's MOOG Theremin
brief_description: Cinema audiences were first introduced to the eerie vibrations of a theremin in the Soviet film Odna (Alone) (1931). During a snowstorm, composer Dimitri Shostakovish amps up the dread with the theremin’s high-pitched wail. Invented in 1920 by Russian physicist Léon Theremin, the instrument works by harnessing electricity and has been used in movies ever since, from The Day the Earth Stood Still (1951) to First Man (2018). In 1932, Australian composer Percy Grainger discovered the instrument (this one is signed by him) and used it to develop compositions that weren’t dictated by scales, rhythms or harmonies.

constellations_primary.name: Good vibrations
constellations_primary.description: Since its invention, the humble theremin has been used in a number of different ways to evoke all sorts of strange sounds and moods.
